data.title: "Dario Is Right," Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Slips as Elon Musk Joins Concerns About AI
data.description:
Given that electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) makes its own artificial intelligence (AI), which is known as Grok, the idea that Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, would express concern about AI development seems like it might be counter-productive. But that happened recently, as Musk joined a growing chorus of concern about AI and where it is going. The news rankled shareholders slightly, and Tesla shares dipped fractionally in Monday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 10.88% loss in its share price over the past year.

"Dario is Right"

Musk took to X, formerly Twitter, to repost a tweet that Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, posted. The tweet connected to a larger essay, which called for a "slowdown of AI development," as noted by a report from Barron's. The AI development slowdown would be used to help pare back some of the risks connected with AI, ranging from economic calamity, bioterrorism operations, and even cyberattacks like the recent Hugging Face hack.

Musk's own comment in response was simple: "Dario is right." This is a strange development, as a lot of Tesla's operations these days depend on AI and AI development. Everything from Grok to the Cybercabs is dependent on a kind of AI development, and for Musk to even indirectly encourage slowdown leaves his company open to disaster.

"Don't Trust Tesla Summon"

Meanwhile, AI-related quotes hit Tesla from another direction, as drivers were encouraged to not trust Tesla Summon. A Tesla driver recently used the feature, which allows the Tesla to drive itself to your current location from a parking lot. But when his Tesla scraped another vehicle while using it, the driver, who a Motor1 report called "Mr. Wang," revealed the damage. The Tesla scraped a substantial gouge in itself, and also damaged an SUV parked next to it.

data.title: Wall Street's Biggest Bear Just Hiked Their S&P 500 Price Target
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) analyst Savita Subramanian hiked her 2026 year-end S&P 500 (SPX) price target to 7,400 from 7,100 on Monday. The target implies downside of 2.6% from current levels and is still the lowest among all Wall Street analysts. In addition, Subramanian issued a 12-month SPX target of 7,800.

Subramanian highlighted several risks, including persistent inflation, higher interest rates, and weak seasonality. September is historically the weakest month of the year with an average loss of 0.6%, according to Carson Group.

BofA Warns of Pullback Risk, Slower Earnings Growth in 2027

Furthermore, Subramanian said that stocks are "overdue for a pullback." She pointed out that the S&P 500 has seen just one 5% pullback this year, compared with a historical average of about three per year. On average, the index faces a 10% or greater correction every year, although the last occurrence of this scenario was in spring 2025.

data.title: AMD Stock Slips Despite a New Deal to Improve AI Trust
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock dipped 5.12% on Monday despite news of a partnership between the semiconductor company and cybersecurity company F-Secure (FSROF). The two companies have shown how their tech can work together to help keep AI-led online activity safe and private. The approach uses model routing to decide where each piece of data should run. It can stay on a device or move to the cloud based on data risk, cost and model needs. F-Secure said it plans to use the setup in its coming TrustPath product.

According to the companies, the need for additional security is growing as AI agents take on more tasks for users. F-Secure said that 84% of people worry that AI makes it hard to know what is real online. It also said 44% are wary of using AI, while only 17% are ready to let an AI agent act for them. TrustPath is built to check each step of an online trip based on its own risk.

"The goal is not to send more events to the largest models," said Jaakko Vainio, senior director at AMD Silo AI. He said the aim is to deal with each event as close to the user as it can. AMD can route less risky tasks to local AI on Ryzen AI chips. More complex or high-risk work can run on AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Instinct GPUs in a private or cloud setup.

F-Secure said TrustPath will treat trust as tied to each step, not a full site. That means a safe site can still have bad or unsafe content. The system can shift the AI route as an agent moves from a public page to a login or payment step.

So Why Was AMD Stock Down Today?

While AMD is making advancements in AI trust, today's news cycle is more focused on the dangers of AI. This came after a warning from Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic. He claimed that AI development needs to slow to allow regulations to catch up. This sparked arguments from several major figures tied to AI, including Elon Musk and President Donald Trump.

data.title: Netflix Stock (NFLX) Climbs as It Joins Amazon and Google to Launch New Streaming Coalition
data.description:
Netflix shares (NFLX) climbed 4% to around $81 on Monday morning. This came as the U.S. streaming giant joined forces with entertainment rivals Amazon (AMZN) and Google-owned (GOOGL) YouTube to launch a new streaming coalition. The tech trade group TechNet leads the alliance. In a statement, TechNet said the coalition "will champion innovation-friendly policies that support consumer choice."

The new group is called the Streaming Access and Choice Alliance (SACA). Notably, NFLX stock also jumped as Evercore analyst Kutgun Maral called Netflix a Buy and lifted his price target to $110. Maral seeks a big opportunity for Netflix to bank on live events to grow its subscriber base.

Why the Move Matters for Netflix

The launch of SACA comes as some observers worry about whether Netflix can maintain audience interest in its streaming service over the long term. To keep boosting engagement and grow its subscriber base, Netflix has been doubling down on live events such as sports and short-form content.

Of note, in July, the streaming giant signed new video licensing deals with multiple digital publishers. It wants to feature their short-form news and entertainment videos on its platform.

However, regulators have turned the spotlight to sports leagues shifting media rights to streaming platforms. For instance, in February, the U.S. Department of Justice and the Federal Communications Commission launched an inquiry into the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961.

Both institutions want to determine whether major sports leagues should continue to enjoy a key antitrust exemption. This exemption allows the leagues to pool together and sell TV rights to their games and events.

"Streaming and digital entertainment companies offer audiences better features and value for their money," TechNet noted in Monday's statement. "The industry and its customers deserve a dedicated voice in Washington, D.C., advocating for policies that enable innovation and address the needs of today's consumers."

Is Netflix a Good Buy Right Now?

data.title: CrowdStrike Stock (CRWD) Soars as AI Risk Arguments Heat Up Today
data.description:
CrowdStrike (CRWD) stock caught the attention of investors on Monday after the company was caught up in a battle over AI advancement. It all started on Saturday, when Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that AI development needs to slow down. The Anthropic CEO has concerns about AI advancing too fast for regulators to properly handle the risks that come with that development.

Amodei's comments on AI elicited a response from CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz. According to an X post from Kurtz, "The frontier will move at whatever speed it moves. The rest of the world will not slow down. Our job in the cybersecurity community is to make sure it moves securely and safely."

Kurtz wasn't the only person to come out against Anthropic's AI advancement warning. Investor Michael Burry also called out the warning as false. Instead, he said the comments made by Amodei and other AI company CEOs were "self-serving." He called such warnings "hype & puffery" designed to make the companies appear "so awesome it could become dangerous." He argued this was to cover up slowing growth ahead of potential initial public offerings (IPOs).

data.title: Disney Stock (NYSE:DIS) Gains as Jimmy Kimmel Talks Begin
data.description:
Entertainment giant Disney (DIS) recently started talks to renew Jimmy Kimmel Live!, a late-night talk show that has landed its share of controversy over political issues. The report from Deadline describing the renewal talks emerged after earlier reports suggested that Kimmel was getting out of the show altogether. But the Deadline report also suggests that Disney may be looking to bring Kimmel's show under tighter rein, and have it cost a lot less. That financial discipline proved welcome to shareholders, as Disney shares gained nearly 2% in Monday morning's trading. Disney has seen a 7.84% loss in its share price over the past year.

Budget Slashing

The talks are likely to be contentious right from the word go, as the report noted that Disney is eager to slash the budget on Kimmel's show. This is increasingly common, as late-night talk shows are a lot less lucrative than they once were. Network television by itself is falling apart, and the interest in staying up to watch it is not holding up either. But Disney's cuts are not specifically aimed at Kimmel, rather at Disney's entire slate of operations.

Disney recently staged layoffs, has more layoffs planned, and has plans to restructure the entire television operation. So paring back Kimmel's show is starting to make a lot more sense to Disney, which will likely be reflected in the talks.

data.title: Google Stock (GOOGL) in Focus as Company Launches Age Verification in Canada
data.description:
Google's parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) says that it will begin identifying underage users in Canada of its online platforms such as YouTube. The technology giant said that it will bring its age assurance technology that employs artificial intelligence (AI) to detect underage users to the Canadian marketplace

"Our age estimation model uses machine learning to interpret a variety of signals already associated with a user's account, such as the types of information a user has searched for or the categories of videos they've watched on YouTube," said Alphabet in a blog post. The move comes in response to Canada's government implementing age restrictions for social media use in the country.

The company says that if the technology identifies someone as underage, their Google account will be changed to include additional protections, such as safeguards on content recommendations.

If it mistakenly identifies an adult as being under 18, the company says that person will be able to prove their age using things like a government ID or a selfie.

"In the coming days, we'll begin to gradually roll out this technology in Canada, carefully monitoring progress as we expand its availability," Jeanette Patell, director of government affairs and public policy at Google Canada, said in the post.

She said the company won't be collecting any new information that isn't already associated with the user's account.

"Age assurance technology is becoming more widely available, and we're encouraged to see its increasing adoption by other companies in recent months," Patell wrote.

"While some would like a system that imposes a universal arbiter of age, we believe that liability and responsibility rest with every service owner — the developer, the publisher, the app creator — because they know their users and services best."

The increasing use of age assurance technology comes as

Meta has already started using AI to identify underage users and place them in teen accounts in Canada. The company said in September it would expand testing of the technology to countries outside the United States., including Canada.

Meta uses AI to look at context clues, such as birthday celebrations, to identify accounts that may be underage. In May, it said it would add "visual analysis" as a technique — which involves AI scanning photos and videos for "visual clues" to a user's age.

Meta promised to implement child protection measures, including stronger measures to identify underage users, as part of a massive recent legal settlement in the United States. But the company has confirmed those changes won't be coming to Canada.

Google's announcement comes after the Liberal government introduced digital safety Bill C-34.

The legislation, which has not yet become law, would force social media platforms to at least temporarily block access for kids under 16. The government has not yet decided how age verification would work and has said it will consult with platforms on specific methods.

In December, Australia became the first country to implement age restrictions for social media. It introduced a law that requires social media platforms to take reasonable steps to keep kids under 16 from using their services. The law doesn't include standards for age verification.

In the United Kingdom, legislation sets out seven separate methods of age verification for legal access to adult content.

They include facial age estimation (which involves a third-party service using a live image to estimate age), a digital ID, or using a credit card, a mobile network operator or a bank to verify age. It also allows for the use of email to estimate age through a process that looks at where an email address has been used previously.

data.title: CoreWeave Stock (CRWV) Drops as Bernstein Analyst Says It's Most Exposed if AI Training Demand Slows
data.description:
CoreWeave (CRWV) stock declined about 7% on Monday after Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei said it could face the biggest risk if AI model development slows. She warned that a shift away from large‑scale training would hit rural data center builds the most. These comments come after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow frontier model capability gains for security reasons. Further, his view was backed by OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk.

Rezaei maintained a Sell rating on CoreWeave stock with a $74 price target, implying 11.1% downside risk.

Here's How CoreWeave Is Exposed to the Slowdown

Rezaei said much of the U.S. data center pipeline was built for training jobs that do not need fast response times. The U.S. has 488 GW of planned nameplate capacity, with about 170 GW seen as real. Around 36% of that sits in rural areas and 34% in Tier 3 markets. This means about 70% of the pipeline is aimed at training or other slow‑latency inference work.

Promotion

If training slows, demand could shift back to Tier 1 metros, which are better built for real‑time inference jobs like agentic workflows, live translation, fraud checks, and robotics.

The analyst noted CoreWeave is the most exposed among the companies under her coverage, as 25% of CoreWeave's active U.S. power sits in Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets. Another nearly 74% of its contracted power is also in Tier 3 and Tier 4. Most of the backlog is take‑or‑pay, so Rezaei does not expect near‑term contract risk. 

However, demand for contracted‑but‑not‑sold rural power could fall if training development slows.

Which Stocks Are Safer

By contrast, Equinix (EQIX), Digital Realty (DLR), and CoreSite are in a stronger spot because almost all of their U.S. capacity sits in top‑tier markets. About 95%, 92%, and 94%, respectively, of their power is in Tier‑1 and Tier‑2 metros, and their future builds also lean toward these areas.

Their dense network links, especially at Equinix, should help keep demand strong as more AI work shifts to fast, real‑time inference.

Is CoreWeave a Good Buy?

Currently, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on CoreWeave stock based on 16 Buys, six Holds, and one Sell. The average CRWV stock price target of $138.81 indicates 67.04% upside potential.
